_goal: error_ceiling: 0 for every schematic by default -- ERC errors hard-fail CI and are essentially never ratcheted. A nonzero error_ceiling is permitted only as a narrowly-scoped, fully-documented exception for a PROVEN tooling artifact (see mcu's _artifact_note); it is not a general debt-paydown ratchet like power_pcb_dataset/drc_ceiling.json's. Every error rule NOT listed in a board's errors_by_type has an implicit ceiling of 0, mirroring drc_ceiling.json's violations_by_type semantics -- a documented allowance for one known error type can never silently cover a new, different one. warning_ceiling may only decrease over time; raising it is a manual, reviewed decision (see scripts/ci_check_erc.py), not an automated one -- there is no separate machine-checked approval contract for this file the way drc_ceiling.json has one (R27/#611); that DRC-specific machinery is intentionally not duplicated here.
_provenance_note: Measured 2026-08-07 on kicad-cli 10.0.5 (the version pinned in .github/docker/ci.Dockerfile, KICAD_VERSION=10.0.5~ubuntu24.04.1), superseding the 2026-07-26 hand-measured 10.0.4 figures (492 warnings/0 errors on temper.kicad_sch, 64 violations on mcu.kicad_sch; docs/STRATEGY.md:1412, :304) that this file previously carried as an unset/TODO placeholder specifically because they were measured on the wrong tool version (see AGENTS.md's DRC-ceiling re-measurement convention and docs/evidence/2026-08-04-router-output-rebaseline-interim.md for why that swap is not safe to assume identical -- a prior DRC ceiling swung +107 on the exact same 10.0.4->10.0.5 PPA move). kicad-cli 10.0.5 was not available via this sandbox's package manager (no root; apt's un-pinned candidate is 7.0.11) or via the pinned ghcr.io/bennetleff/temper-ci:latest container (docker pull failed repeatedly: 'failed to register layer: exit status 22: unpigz: abort: zlib version less than 1.2.3', a host-level unpigz/zlib incompatibility). Obtained instead by downloading the kicad-10.0-releases PPA's kicad_10.0.5~ubuntu24.04.1_amd64.deb and kicad-footprints .deb plus the missing runtime deps (libgit2-1.7, libnng1, the libocct-*-7.6t64 family, libmbedtls14t64/libmbedx509-1t64, libhttp-parser2.9, libwxgtk-webview3.2-1t64 -- all from the standard Ubuntu 24.04 archive, no PPA needed for the deps) with `apt-get download` (no root required) and extracting every .deb with `dpkg-deb -x` into a userspace root, then running the extracted kicad-cli with LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointed at the extracted lib dirs. `kicad-cli version` reports '10.0.5'. Every count below was verified stable across 10 repeated runs each (zero variance in aggregate or per-type counts) before being trusted as a ceiling.

boards._artifact_note: The 20 pin_not_connected 'errors' are NOT real circuit defects -- they are a proven artifact of running kicad-cli sch erc on mcu.kicad_sch STANDALONE. mcu.kicad_sch is a SUB-SHEET of pcb/temper.kicad_sch (referenced via a Sheetfile property at temper.kicad_sch:516), not an independent root schematic -- there is no pcb/mcu.kicad_pro. Checked in isolation, its hierarchical labels (e.g. '+3V3', 'V_BUS_SENSE', 'I_SENSE') have no parent sheet to resolve against, and kicad-cli reports each as "Hierarchical label '<name>' in root sheet cannot be connected to non-existent parent sheet" -- a tooling limitation of checking a subsheet outside its hierarchy, not a finding about the mcu circuit. PROOF this is an artifact, not a real defect: the temper.kicad_sch entry above (the correct, hierarchy-aware ERC run, which recursively covers every subsheet including mcu.kicad_sch) reports 0 errors and none of these hierarchical-label messages anywhere in its 498 warnings -- verified by grepping the temper.kicad_sch report for the same label names and 'non-existent parent', zero matches. This board is still gated (rather than dropped, per the plan's explicit 'run ERC against both schematics' instruction and STRATEGY.md's precedent of measuring mcu.kicad_sch separately) so that a genuinely NEW error type on mcu.kicad_sch -- which errors_by_type's implicit-zero-ceiling semantics still catch -- is not silently absorbed into this ceiling. Recommended follow-up for a maintainer: either stop gating mcu.kicad_sch standalone (temper.kicad_sch's hierarchical run already covers its real connectivity) or teach kicad-cli sch erc to accept subsheet context, whichever is preferred; until then this documented ceiling is the honest alternative to either a permanently-red gate or a false '0 errors' claim.
